news_analysis.headline_hook: The 'Instagram IPO' Trap: How Cyber Criminals Are Exploiting Retail Pre-IPO Greed
news_analysis.breaking_event_summary: Police in Sikar have registered four major cyber fraud cases, including a prominent scam where victims were tricked into sending funds for fake 'Instagram IPO' allocations.
news_analysis.retail_illusion: Retail investors falsely believe that private social media groups, Instagram ads, or grey-market brokers can grant 'guaranteed early access' or 'VIP allotments' to upcoming high-profile IPOs.
news_analysis.institutional_reality: No legitimate IPO allotment in India occurs outside SEBI-mandated ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount) via certified bank/broker channels. Private UPI transfers to third parties for IPO shares are 100% illicit fraud mechanisms.
news_analysis.actionable_retail_rule: Never transfer capital to any personal or corporate UPI/bank account for an IPO; legitimate IPO funds are only blocked in your own bank account via SEBI-ASBA.

slides.title: The Fake Instagram IPO Trap
slides.subtitle: How cyber criminals exploit retail pre-IPO greed.

slides.title: The Pre-IPO Allotment Myth
slides.card_text: Retail investors believe private messaging groups or social ads offer exclusive IPO access. In Sikar, 4 cyber frauds exposed this illusion. Legitimate Indian IPO allocations occur exclusively via SEBI-mandated ASBA channels, where capital remains blocked in your personal bank account.

slides.title: How Fake VIP Allotments Work
slides.card_text: Fraudulent brokers direct victims to transfer funds into personal or corporate UPI accounts under the guise of 100% guaranteed allocation. Once capital leaves your personal bank via direct transfer, it bypasses clearing corporations and is immediately laundered across untraceable accounts.

slides.title: How Scammers Capture Capital
slides.card_text: Real pre-IPO secondary transactions require unlisted share demat transfers via regulated depository participants. Scammers spoof institutional order books using fake dashboards, capturing 100% principal loss before trading ever occurs on registered exchanges like NSE or BSE.

slides.title: Understanding Total Capital Loss
slides.card_text: Yield chasers seeking speculative gains face a complete downside asymmetry: a 100% loss on unverified IPO transfers requires an impossible infinity return to recover lost principal. Fraudulent transfers completely destroy long-term portfolio compounding velocity instantly.

slides.title: The Mandatory ASBA Rule
slides.card_text: Never transfer capital directly to third-party UPI or corporate bank accounts for primary equity offerings. Legitimate IPO funds are strictly blocked inside your own bank account using SEBI-ASBA until final allotment confirmation occurs.

slides.title: The Pre-Trade Verification Protocol
slides.card_text: Before allocating capital to any public offer: 1. Verify SEBI registration of the intermediary; 2. Demand ASBA blocking through your bank net-banking portal; 3. Reject external UPI links or private account transfer requests outright.
